configuration.title: RulealizeStudio.Avalonia
configuration.plugins.description: The folder of vocabularies a rule set is compiled against, relative to the rule set's own folder. Empty means the application's build output, 'bin/Debug/net10.0', beside a project, whose build puts there the vocabularies the project lists; and otherwise 'plugin', where 'rulealize restore' puts them.
configuration.server.description: RulealizeStudio.Server.dll. Empty means the one inside the extension; run from its repository, the one built there.
configuration.feed.description: A folder of packages a new application restores RulealizeStudio's libraries from, while they are not on nuget.org. Empty means the ones inside the extension; run from its repository, feed/ there, where packing them puts them.
configuration.ruledger.description: The ruledger command, which says what changed about what is legal and derives the design again. Empty means ruledger 1.4.0, fetched into the extension's own folder, after asking, the first time it is needed.
configuration.rulealize.description: The rulealize command, which fetches the vocabularies a rule set on its own requires. Empty means rulealize 0.13.0, fetched into the extension's own folder, after asking, the first time it is needed.
view.walkthrough.name: Walkthrough
viewsWelcome.walkthrough:
From an empty folder to an application read as its test cases on its own window.
[Open the walkthrough](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22reny-develop.rulealizestudio-avalonia%23rules%22%5D)
view.application.name: Application
viewsWelcome.noFolder:
An application is a folder. Open one to make it in, or make it wherever you say.
[Open a folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
[New application](command:rulealize.application)
Not sure where to begin? [Walkthrough](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22reny-develop.rulealizestudio-avalonia%23rules%22%5D)
viewsWelcome.noApplication:
There is no application here yet. Make one — a window with nothing on it, and a specification to write — or start from an example that has its rules already.
[New application](command:rulealize.application)
[Start from an example](command:rulealize.start?%5B%22example%2FCountdown%22%5D)
Not sure where to begin? [Walkthrough](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22reny-develop.rulealizestudio-avalonia%23rules%22%5D)
walkthrough.rules.title: An application, read on its own screen
walkthrough.rules.description: From an empty folder to an application's test cases read on its own window, a change asked of your agent, and what that change did — without reading JSON or XAML.
walkthrough.rules.folder.title: Open a folder
walkthrough.rules.folder.description:
An application is a folder, kept the way everything else in it is.
[Open a folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
walkthrough.rules.start.title: Start from an example
walkthrough.rules.start.description:
Makes an example application in the folder — its rules, its screen, what it should do and its test design — builds it, and shows it in the RulealizeStudio.Avalonia view.
[Start from an example](command:rulealize.start?%5B%22example%2FCountdown%22%5D)
walkthrough.rules.screens.title: Read its test cases
walkthrough.rules.screens.description:
Every situation the rules can reach is a test case: the steps that reach it on the application's own window, and what the window should be after them.
[Show its test cases](command:rulealize.screens)
walkthrough.rules.change.title: Ask for a change
walkthrough.rules.change.description: Commit the example as it is first, in Source Control: what a change did is read against what was last committed. Then ask your agent for a change — to count to twelve, say — and read what it did at the top of the test cases, where it stays until you commit it.
walkthrough.rules.own.title: Make your own
walkthrough.rules.own.description:
An application of your own, from nothing: a window with nothing on it and a specification to write. Everything about it is in the RulealizeStudio.Avalonia view in the activity bar.
[New application](command:rulealize.application)
